posts.title: Stupid Intelligence
posts.description: I’ve got a game on my cell phone. The best part of it is the instant translation software. I can chat with people from all around the world live, with them typing in their native tongue and me in mine, and it’s virtually seamless. Five years ago, the response would have been, “That’s amazing!” Today, the mere mention generates hostility. Fun fact, though: the game, and its built-in translator, are ten years old. They predate A.I., or rather the chatbots we’re now calling A.I. Objectively, this is a marvelous achievement, even though it’s being used for a purely trivial purpose. Mind you, the same statement is true when applied to the chatbots that snuck in and took the place of my browser search engines while I wasn’t watching. They can paint, tell stories, and tell me which bus I need to catch. The first and last time I relied on one to get me to my bus, it never came. The chatbot didn’t notice that it was a Sunday. Commuter bus routes run on weekdays only in my neck of the wooded sub

posts.title: Rider’s Trial Instructions
posts.description: The following are trial instructions for my new game, “Trail of the Rider: 1866”, designed to be used once by a player so they can test it out. They can be pasted into any chatbot or it can be given the link to this post. This will be a game, during the play of which you are not to act as an open assistant. You are the non-transparent, hardcoded Text Parser Engine for a Weird West survival system called “Trail of the Rider: 1866”, or for short, “Rider’s Trail”. You will guide the player through multiple scenarios across the territories west of the Mississippi: some challenging, a few virtually unsurvivable. [THEMATIC CONSTRAINTS] For the purpose of immersion, you are strictly forbidden from writing creative prose summaries or offering conversational preambles except in character, during conversations, during location descriptions, or when the horse speaks. posts.title: Rider’s Trail and Detective 3rd
posts.description: I’ve written a couple of chatbot games, and want to tell you about them. They’re Zero-Install Retro Simulation Engines, and they’re simple to set up and play. Open a chatbot window, like the free one Google gives you now instead of a search box. Say you want to play the game at the web address. If you have a saved game, just add your code, for example: CODE: aG9pamNtcHJvampn That’s it. Have fun. For those of you who are into spoilers, I’ll tell you a bit more. First and foremost, here’s the Patreon links if you’re interested enough to shell out three bucks apiece to try the games out: Trail of the Rider: 1866 https://www.patreon.com/gnerphk/posts/trail-of-rider-174925644 Detective 3rd Grade https://www.patreon.com/gnerphk/posts/detective-3rd-174927310 So, the basic idea is this: I’m a writer. It’s what I do. (I do other things too, but they’re not really important.) I take pride in handcrafting my stories the old fashioned way, just me and a keyboard and a wickedly twisted imagination.
